bot_short_squeeze_v1.method: Live config: capital 10,000 (bots/short_squeeze/config.py:11); fixed-R 1% over the swept-low stop, notional capped at 3x (config.py:36-37; botlib.py:555-577): notional = min(0.01/risk_pct, 3) * 10000 with risk_pct = (entry - low*0.999)/entry in perp terms (strategy/config.py:57-63; signal.py:475-481) - mean 2.497x, 31 of 71 at the cap; stop = trigger low x 0.999, target 3R, time stop 6h (signal.py:481); stop before target (signal.py:337-359); booked cost 10 bp RT + 0 slippage on notional (strategy/config.py:68,77; signal.py:282-286) and funding (apply_funding=True). Live trade selection reproduced from raw triggers: skip while this variant holds a position (signal.py:462-466), skip within 4h of the last TAKEN trade (cooldown keyed on execute time, signal.py:376-380 and 541), else take; 133 raw triggers -> 71 taken (62 skipped: 10 open, 52 cooldown). This is exactly the research pool: research cooldown on the recomputed raw mask reproduces the S1 71 with zero differences, and the live-semantics set is the same 71. Per trade: value = [N*pnl_frac - N*10/1e4 + N*F/100] / 10000 * 100, N = notional, F = LONG funding over (entry, exit] with funding.accrued_pct semantics (funding.py:112-118,138); exit = entry+6h for time exits (live semantics) else close of the exit 1 m bar. Mean decomposition (% capital/trade): price +0.3181, cost -0.2497, funding -0.0004 (mean net R vs reference stop +0.162). Exit kinds: 39 stop, 21 target, 11 time. Resampled 10th percentile of the mean (iid, 20k, seed 42) at n=5/10/20/30: -0.742 / -0.516 / -0.353 / -0.274.
bot_short_squeeze_v1.caveats: (1) Research exit model (1 m spot high/low touch, level fills, perp levels on the spot path) vs live 60 s close polling filling at the close, with entry booked at the perp 15m close and exit at the spot 1 m close. Entry basis perp-vs-spot at these triggers: mean -5.1 bp (sd 1.9), so live books a ~+5 bp-of-notional artefact on every trade (about +0.13% of capital at 2.5x), partly offset by close-poll stop fills below the level; poll-model sensitivity n 70, mean +0.104 vs +0.068. With median stop width 0.34% of entry this matters more here than for squeeze_bull. (2) Cost is 3.7x the net mean: the reference is dominated by the cost line, and any booked-cost change moves it one-for-one. (3) Cooldown edge: 2 of the 71 taken trades fire exactly 16 bars after the previous taken trade; live compares (now - last) < 4h using tick timestamps with seconds, so these can be blocked live depending on jitter. (4) Live signal approximations not modelled: daily-frozen 90d percentile snapshot vs per-bar window (calibration log: 0% gate flips) and post-2026-04-13 single-settlement funding in the macro gate. (5) Research time exit is the close of the bar opening at entry+6h (entry+6h01m) vs live entry+6h: a 1-minute difference in exit price. (6) Funding pre-2026-04-25 from hourly predicted-rate rows at 8h boundaries (live semantics, unverified vs settlements); negligible at 6h holds. (7) Live trades closed before 2026-09-12 booked 25 bp (docs/calibration/short_squeeze.md:79-80); exclude them. (8) 71 trades over 4 years, clustered on 62 short-macro days - resampled trades are not independent in time.
bot_short_squeeze_v1.notes:
What these numbers are. Each value is one research trade under the live bot's current sizing and booked costs: net pnl_usdt / 10,000 * 100. That is the same unit as the dashboard's live metric. Costs are the booked 7 bp (squeeze_bull) and 10 bp (short_squeeze) on notional, charged once (trades.py:342). Funding is added using the live function's own query (funding.py:112-118,138). Trades are filtered to what one position per variant allows, and each list is in exit order (one open position means entry order equals exit order). Nothing was tuned. No repo file, prod.db or process was touched: prod.db was opened mode=ro only, and all output is in the scratchpad.

Per-trade outcomes. squeeze_bull uses the saved S1 walks in studies/notebooks/sizing_style_2026_09/results/s1_trades.csv (P0_shipped and P1b_target_only). short_squeeze needed a recompute for one reason: the live cooldown counts from the last TAKEN trade (bots/short_squeeze/strategy/signal.py:376-380 and 541), while the research cooldown counts from every trigger (exec_lib.py:359). I rebuilt the raw trigger mask with a verbatim copy of exec_lib.short_squeeze_frame and walked it with sizing_lib.run_policy. The research cooldown on that mask reproduces the S1 71 exactly, and every re-walked trade matches the saved pnl_frac to 1e-12.

Summary (mean % of capital per trade / win rate / n):
- bot_squeeze_bull_v1: +0.284 / 58% / 117
- bot_squeeze_bull_nostop_v1: +0.426 / 67% / 103
- bot_short_squeeze_v1: +0.068 / 44% / 71
- bot_short_squeeze_nostop_v1: +0.027 / 63% / 62
Each variant's caveats list the iid 10th percentile of resampled means at n = 5/10/20/30. At n = 10 they are -0.160 / -0.057 / -0.516 / -0.628, so an AMBER rule needs a minimum n or it will almost never fire.

Biggest approximation, same for all four. The values use the research exit model: 1 m spot high/low touches, filled at the level, in perp terms. Live polls the last closed 1 m spot close every 60 s, fills at that close, and books a perp entry against a spot exit. I re-ran a sensitivity with that live polling model. Live-style means come out higher on every variant: +0.310 / +0.454 / +0.104 / +0.075. The two short_squeeze gaps are mainly perp entries averaging -5.1 bp vs spot. So the reference is conservative in the sense that it will not cause false AMBERs, but it slightly weakens the warning. The poll model is my own re-derivation, not study code, so it is only a sensitivity.

Findings worth your attention (observations, nothing changed):
(a) bot_short_squeeze_nostop_v1 is close to break-even in dollars at 1x notional even though its R mean is +0.80. Its edge sits in the tight-stop triggers that fixed-R sizing levered up. The '~1/2.5 of the stop variant's dollars' comment (bots/short_squeeze/config.py:41) does not hold: this variant earns less per trade than the stop variant.
(b) Live paper P&L mixes venues: entry at the perp close (squeeze_bull signal.py:242; short_squeeze signal.py:475) and exit at the btc_1m spot close (price_feed.py:14-16, 79-88). The recut_lib divergence check (D4) splits out funding and backstop cost but not this basis, which is about 5 bp of notional on short_squeeze.
(c) One squeeze_bull fire (trigger bar 2023-03-24 11:00) has perp 186 bp below spot. It is kept as the study walked it.
(d) docs/calibration/squeeze_bull.md:125 dates the S1 pool '2022-01 → 2026-06'; the fires actually run 2022-03-25 → 2026-09-04.

Comparing against live. Exclude, or flag, live trades booked before 2026-09-12 (15 bp squeeze_bull, 25 bp short_squeeze). Also flag SJ-4250 (47 h hold under the old time-stop schedule).

Working tree. While I worked, another session had uncommitted edits in botlib.py, both runners and strategies/trades.py. They route the scheduled-exit backstop through each sleeve's own close function and add a guard for close races. They do not change sizing, costs or funding for normal sweep closes, so the baseline is unaffected. The running processes still use whatever code they loaded at start. No mutation-drill entries are proposed; this task changes no code.

bot_short_squeeze_nostop_v1.method: Live config: use_stop False (bots/short_squeeze/config.py:26); fixed notional NOSTOP_NOTIONAL_X 1.0 = $10,000 (config.py:43; runner.py:66-84); no stop, no target, 6h time stop only (signal.py:496-502, _stop_price/_target_price None); single-open (signal.py:462-466) and 4h cooldown from the last taken trade (signal.py:376-380, 541) - with a 6h hold the open guard always binds first (133 raw -> 62 taken, 71 skipped as position_open); 10 bp RT booked on notional + funding (strategy/config.py:68,77; signal.py:282-286). Per trade: value = [10000*pnl_frac - 10000*10/1e4 + 10000*F/100] / 10000 * 100 = pnl_frac*100 - 0.10 + F, F = LONG funding over (entry, entry+6h] with funding.accrued_pct semantics (funding.py:112-118,138). Mean decomposition (% capital/trade): price +0.1264, cost -0.1000, funding +0.0002 (mean net R vs the swept-low reference distance +0.80). Resampled 10th percentile of the mean (iid, 20k, seed 42) at n=5/10/20/30: -0.898 / -0.628 / -0.440 / -0.350.
bot_short_squeeze_nostop_v1.caveats: (1) This differs from S3b's single-open set (n 59): S3b applied single-open to the research-cooldown pool, while the live bot's cooldown is keyed on taken trades, which admits 3 triggers and drops others. (2) At 1x fixed notional the dollar expectancy is near break-even (+0.027% of capital per trade), even though the R mean is +0.80. On the 71-trade S1 P1 pool the unweighted mean move is +0.139% of notional, but weighted by fixed-R notional it is +0.292%: the no-stop edge sits in the tight-stop triggers that fixed-R sized up. So the comment 'dollars are ~1/2.5 of the stop variant's' (bots/short_squeeze/config.py:41) and docs/calibration/short_squeeze.md:84-87 overstate this variant's dollar result. Here it earns less per trade than the stop variant (+0.068). Observation only, nothing changed. (3) Live mixed-venue booking: entry at the perp 15m close (mean 5.1 bp below spot at these triggers), exit at the spot 1 m close, so live gains ~+0.05% of capital per trade at 1x. Poll-model sensitivity: n 62, mean +0.075 vs +0.027 here, almost all of it that basis term. With a mean this close to zero, that artefact is half of the gap between the reference and zero. (4) Heavy left tail: worst trade -6.74% of capital (the -7.8 R replay trade); resampled means at small n are very wide. (5) Research time exit is 1 minute later than live (close of the bar opening at entry+6h). (6) Live signal approximations and funding caveats as for the stop variant. (7) Variant live only since 2026-09-12.
